Render Stan Prior Density Accumulation

Source: R/JointModel.R
stan_prior_density.Rd

Converts the continuous prior statements used by jmpost into explicit log-density evaluations for the generated quantities block.

Usage

stan_prior_density(code)

Arguments

code

(string) Stan model-block contents containing only prior contributions. The caller must remove likelihood contributions before calling this function.

Value

A length-one character vector containing Stan statements that accumulate the joint log prior in lprior.

Details

Sampling statements of the form x ~ distribution(arguments); become lprior += distribution_lpdf(x | arguments);. Distributions with no arguments, such as std_normal(), omit the vertical bar. Explicit target += statements are redirected to lprior, retaining adjustments such as transformed-prior Jacobians. Line comments starting with // are removed; surrounding braced control flow and local declarations are retained.

The model block already evaluates these priors for sampling. Re-evaluating them in generated quantities deliberately adds work once per saved draw to keep the extra logging calculation out of HMC leapfrog and gradient evaluations. The original sampling statements also let Stan omit terms that are constant with respect to the parameters. Computing lprior in transformed parameters and adding it to target would avoid the repeated prior evaluation when saving draws, but would evaluate the full logged density at every leapfrog step. Likelihood outputs reuse the existing likelihood evaluations and only add aggregation.

For truncation with scalar bounds (T[lower, upper], including either one-sided form), the output subtracts the log normalising probability for each element of x. Lower-only truncation uses the log complementary CDF, upper-only truncation uses the log CDF, and two-sided truncation uses log_diff_exp() of the two log CDFs. Distribution arguments are accessed elementwise, broadcasting scalars and length-one vectors. The loop is guarded so that an empty vector contributes zero. Parameter-dependent normalisation, such as that of a bounded horseshoe prior, is therefore retained.

This helper handles the well-formed continuous prior syntax emitted by the package templates, rather than arbitrary Stan programs. Sampling statements must end in semicolons; control-flow bodies must be braced. Block comments, discrete distributions and brace-delimited array literals are unsupported. The caller must declare and initialise lprior and include the prior_density_size() and prior_density_element() overloads from base/functions.stan when truncation is present. The original model code is not modified by this conversion.

See also

stan_density_arguments()
